segments.text: Level two's telnet service hands out another rot-thirteen challenge, and the level2 box hides the next hop. The goal is the level4 password from /pass/level4.
The service prints GungJnfRnfl; tr rot-thirteen decodes it to ThatWasEasy.
I log in as level2 with the previous password and confirm the identity.
The README points at a backdoor hidden somewhere on the system.

A find for setuid-root-style binaries sweeps the box and turns up two unusual entries: the level3 backdoor in var opt, and a level4 backdoor in var local whose name is a dot, six spaces, and level4 underscore backdoor.
The listing confirms it: dash r w s r-xr-x, setuid level4, group level3.
Running it drops a shell whose id shows euid one thousand four, level4, and the pass file reads n three x t underscore l three v three l exclamation.
